BREAKING: Russia extends its diesel export ban until the end of Oct. While the measure was largely expected, it would further tighten the global diesel market.

EUROPE’s gasoil prices have climbed to one of the highest levels on record even after adjusting for inflation. Front-month gasoil futures have averaged more than €1270 per tonne so far in September, the third highest on record after October and June 2022, and higher than during the oil price spike in 2008. The continued disruption of crude and fuel exports through the Strait of Hormuz combined with Ukraine’s attacks on Russia’s oil refineries and the relative weakness of the euro against the dollar have all contributed to near-record high prices. The threat of an outright ban or restrictions on U.S. diesel exports has intensified the upward pressure:

Asking for a friend. 

If oil refuses to go down while 1) everyone is touting flows are back to normal and 2) US released the last tranche of the SPR, what does that mean?

EIA reported in its petroleum supply monthly today that US crude oil production hit 13.948 million b/d. 

But if you look at the adjustment, it was -0.469 million b/d, which implies that US crude oil production was overstated. 

Effective production is 13.479 million b/d. 

This is the 3rd consecutive month of negative supply adjustment.

EIA reported materially lower refinery throughput than our estimate contributing to the delta (16.257 vs 16.7, 3.1 million bbls). 

Meanwhile, lower refinery throughput is translating to much lower product storage. 

Given how low inventories are today, we have no cushion left.

Indian oil refiners are hiring tankers to sail through the Strait of Hormuz to pick up crude from within the Persian Gulf, a change of tactics to help them cut costs and secure their supply chains.

Processors have issued tenders and are negotiating with shipping lines, according to people familiar with their efforts. So far, Sinokor Group and Dynacom Tankers Management Ltd. have been awarded tenders, said the people, asking not to be named as they’re not authorized to speak to media. As China looks to safeguard domestic supplies, state oil major PetroChina cancelled on Wednesday the majority of its gasoline and jet fuel shipmenets planned for October three of the sources said.

Energy delivered another strong month despite the recent retracement, gaining 8.5% and helping offset losses across all other major sectors, most notably precious metals at –6.2% and soft commodities at –8.5%.

At the individual level, Brent and gasoil gained around 12.5%, while the biggest losses were seen in cocoa at –20%, cotton –15%, wheat –10% and silver –8%. Notably, the steep backwardation across energy markets provided a substantial boost to total returns: excluding the positive roll yield, the BCOM Energy Spot Index gained only 4.8%, compared with the 8.3% total-return gain.
